entries.clue: Put down in crude motel (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' says the answer lies inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

annotation.surface: A grumble about a seedy roadside motel you were put in for the night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crude motel' reads as the thing being put down, but it is only the carrier: the answer runs across the gap between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of lowering someone's rank, not the sense of insulting them that the surface suggests.

entries.clue: A seed is sown, producing a social evil (7)

indicatorNotes.is sown: sown seed is scattered over the ground, so the letters are scattered too

annotation.surface: A parable-like line: one bad seed planted grows into something that blights society.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'is' does double work: it is part of the fodder, and with 'sown' it makes the indicator read naturally.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a canker spreading through society is called a disease, as in 'the disease of corruption'.

entries.clue: Jerry’s manually controlled device? (5)

blocks.note: the cartoon Jerry, Tom's small rodent adversary
a computer pointer moved around the desk by hand

annotation.surface: A question about some gadget belonging to someone called Jerry.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is', not possession: Jerry of Tom and Jerry is a mouse, and so is the thing on your desk you steer by hand.
annotation.definitionFit: One definition by example (a famous cartoon mouse), one by description (the computer peripheral, the question mark flagging the stretch).

entries.clue: So the sports official has valuable material (9)

blocks.note: ore is rock mined for its metal

annotation.surface: A deduction that the referee must own something precious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'So' opens the clue like a conversational filler, but it is the whole definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words introduce a consequence drawn from what went before.

entries.clue: Male chiefs made to look silly with female about (7)

indicatorNotes.to look silly: MADE is made a fool of, its letters knocked into a silly order
indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means surrounding, so HEN goes round the jumble

blocks.note: hen = female bird; goes round the outside

annotation.surface: Pompous male leaders humiliated by a woman standing nearby.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Made' looks like part of the story's grammar, but it is the fodder; the jumble sits inside HEN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a headman is the chief of a village or tribe, and the clue's 'male' matches the -MEN ending.

entries.clue: This singer has absorbed such an audible sound of disapproval (7)

indicatorNotes.has absorbed: something absorbed is taken inside, so the answer is soaked up within these words

annotation.surface: A performer who has soaked up the audience's jeers.
annotation.walkthrough: The singer seems to be the one taking the boos; in fact 'this singer' just holds the answer across its word break.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: hissing is the noise an audience makes to show it disapproves, as at a pantomime villain.

entries.clue: A revolutionary fighter’s pains (5)

annotation.surface: The wounds or hardships of some guerrilla soldier.
annotation.walkthrough: Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both plural nouns for dull bodily hurts; the surface makes 'pains' look like hardships instead.

entries.clue: Stiltedness of two maidens – Queen Anne is keeping them apart (9)

indicatorNotes.keeping them apart: what keeps two things apart stands between them, so the middle chunk separates the two maidens

blocks.note: m = maiden (over) in cricket scoring; one M each end

annotation.surface: Two prim girls being kept separate by a disapproving Queen Anne.
annotation.walkthrough: A maiden is a cricket over with no runs scored, written M on the scorecard; the surface's young ladies are a decoy.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: mannerism is affected, artificial style in art or speech, which is what stiltedness describes.

entries.clue: Eccentric person receiving disrespect is one in birthday suit (6)

indicatorNotes.receiving: one who receives takes something in, so NUT takes the insult inside itself

blocks.note: a nut = a crank; split around the insert
dis = slang for disrespect, sits inside NU…T

annotation.surface: An oddball who gets sneered at turns out to be naked.
annotation.walkthrough: In your birthday suit is an idiom for naked, as on the day you were born.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone in their birthday suit wears nothing, and a naturist does so by choice.

entries.clue: Lively agent grabbing a bit of sleep (6)

indicatorNotes.grabbing: to grab is to seize and hold, so SPY holds NAP inside it

blocks.note: a secret agent; split around the insert
a nap is a short sleep; sits inside S…PY

annotation.surface: A spy on the job manages to snatch forty winks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lively agent' reads as one phrase; the definition is only the first word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in a snappy tune or a snappy pace: brisk and full of energy.

entries.clue: Nurses eat out – wine provided (9)

indicatorNotes.out: 'out' as in out of order: the letters are put out of place

annotation.surface: Nurses on a night out at a restaurant, with the wine included.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' is a natural phrase, which hides 'out' as the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Sauternes is one particular sweet white wine, from Bordeaux.

entries.clue: Honorary Editor now with a sharp edge presumably (5)

annotation.definition: now with a sharp edge presumably
annotation.surface: An honorary editor who has become cutting in his remarks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Honorary Editor' looks like a job title, but splits into two abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a blade that has been sharpened on a whetstone now has an edge; 'presumably' hedges the inference.

entries.clue: A river in which to find large woman (5)

indicatorNotes.in which to find: the river is the place in which the next item is found, so L goes inside it

blocks.note: the Dee, a river in Wales, England and Scotland; split around the insert
L = large, as on clothes labels; sits inside DE…E

annotation.surface: A river where a big woman might be found swimming.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large woman' sounds like a pair, but 'large' is L and 'woman' is the definition alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a woman's first name stands for any woman, a loose but common crossword device.

entries.clue: Religious lady snoops, tragic female in novel (9)

blocks.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Thomas Hardy's tragic heroine

annotation.surface: A list of female characters: a pious lady, a busybody, a doomed heroine.
annotation.walkthrough: The commas make three people; really 'snoops' is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a woman who officiates in a religion's rites, as in ancient temples.

entries.clue: Pleasant sounds from organisation UK left not to be trusted? (7)

annotation.definitionNote: euphony is a singular mass noun; the clue's plural means the same pleasantness of sound

blocks.note: the European Union, which the UK left in 2020

annotation.surface: A Brexit jab: the EU makes sweet noises that shouldn't be trusted.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is political, with Brexit as the key to EU; the question mark hedges PHONY as 'not to be trusted'.
annotation.definitionFit: From Greek for 'good sound': a formal word for harmonious, agreeable sound.

entries.clue: Polite remark with dismissal of fifty lowly workers (9)

indicatorNotes.with dismissal of: dismissing someone sends them away, so the L is sent out of the word

blocks.note: a pleasantry is a polite remark

annotation.surface: A manager politely sacking fifty workers on the shop floor.
annotation.walkthrough: The dismissal sounds like workers being fired, but what goes is the Roman fifty.
annotation.definitionFit: A description of a class: the peasantry are poor farm labourers, collectively the lowest rung of rural society.

entries.clue: Go to have second drink and chat (6)

blocks.note: a sip is a small drink

annotation.surface: An invitation to stay for another round and a natter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second drink' reads as a refill; 'second' is just S.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both as a noun and a verb: idle talk, often about other people.

entries.clue: Unusual insect is beginning to tantalise lab worker? (9)

indicatorNotes.Unusual: an unusual arrangement is one out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A strange bug catching a researcher's eye in the laboratory.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that plenty of scientists never set foot in a lab.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the typical scientist works in a laboratory, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Component of brief agenda – final bit of little importance? (3,3)

indicatorNotes.Component of: a component is a part, so the answer is a part of the words that follow

annotation.surface: The last item on a short meeting agenda, the one nobody cares about.
annotation.walkthrough: A fag end is British for a cigarette stub, and so the useless last remnant of anything; the surface's meeting agenda is exactly such a tail.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom extended from the cigarette butt: the fag end of a day or a meeting is its last, dreary part.

entries.clue: Men confused in gloomy country (7)

indicatorNotes.confused: confused things are mixed up, so MEN's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: dark = gloomy; split around the insert

annotation.surface: Men wandering lost in some dismal land.
annotation.walkthrough: A nod to Hamlet, the gloomy Dane: 'something is rotten in the state of Denmark'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Denmark is one example of a country.

entries.clue: Mysteries in games being played (7)

indicatorNotes.being played: letters being played with are toyed with and moved around

annotation.surface: Puzzles that come up during games in progress.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from Greek for riddle, anything puzzling or hard to explain.

entries.clue: More than one twister in deed is found out (6)

indicatorNotes.found out: 'out' as in out of order, so the letters are knocked out of place

annotation.surface: A cheat whose dishonest act has been exposed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twister' suggests a swindler, and 'found out' backs that up; here it is a swirl of water.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful description: an eddy is a small whirling current, something that twists, and the plural matches 'more than one'.

entries.clue: Rocky Isle is a location on old European map (7)

indicatorNotes.Rocky: rocky means shaky or unsteady, so the letters are shaken up

annotation.surface: A rocky island marked on an antique map of Europe.
annotation.walkthrough: Silesia is a region now split mostly between Poland and the Czech Republic; 'old' because it no longer exists as a state.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: Silesia was a historic province of Prussia and Austria, seen on older maps of central Europe.

entries.clue: Mischief-makers quietly participating in tricks (6)

indicatorNotes.participating in: one participating in something is inside it, so P goes into SCAMS

blocks.note: scams = tricks; split around the insert
p = piano, quietly in music; sits inside SCAM…S

annotation.surface: Troublemakers slipping silently into some con.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quietly' reads as how they join in, but it is P.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: scamps are rascals, usually affectionately said of mischievous children.

entries.clue: Charlie hurried, being humiliated (9)

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Charlie rushing off, red-faced.
annotation.walkthrough: Charlie looks like a person's name, but is just C.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: chastened means subdued and humbled by a rebuke, close to humiliated.

entries.clue: Part of body doctor sometimes holds (5)

indicatorNotes.holds: the words hold the answer the way a hand holds an object, inside them

annotation.surface: A body part a doctor sometimes grips during an examination.
annotation.walkthrough: The doctor seems to be doing the holding; it is the words that hold the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the trunk, without head or limbs, is one part of the body.

entries.clue: One missing love, friend in the country (5)

indicatorNotes.missing: something missing a part is without it, so ONE loses its O

blocks.note: ONE minus O; love = O, zero in tennis

annotation.surface: A lonely heartbroken person with only a friend, away in the countryside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The country' reads as rural life, not a nation.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a Himalayan kingdom turned republic, one of the world's nations.

entries.clue: Demure adult is first in Rome (5)

blocks.note: A = adult, the old film certificate

annotation.surface: A modest grown-up ranks top in Rome.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In Rome' asks for Italian: the feminine form, familiar from prima donna and prima ballerina.
annotation.definitionFit: A foreign-language sense: 'in Rome' flags the Italian word for first.

entries.clue: Mum is chum, right? (5)

annotation.surface: Checking that your mother is really your friend.
annotation.walkthrough: The question reads as doubt about a friendship; 'right' is just R.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional, dated use: Latin for mother, as old-fashioned British public-school slang for one's mum.

entries.clue: Word of prayer – it is full of energy in services (9)

indicatorNotes.is full of: something full of a thing has it inside, so IS is filled with E

blocks.note: used as it stands; split around the insert
e = energy, as in E=mc²; sits inside I…S

annotation.surface: A church scene: a prayer ending with gusto at a service.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Services' in the surface are church services; the definition means facilities.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of useful facilities a place offers, not the church sense the surface points at.

entries.clue: Shakespearean villain reticent, having shut up (7)

blocks.note: to lock is to shut up securely

annotation.surface: A villain on stage who has gone quiet and clammed up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' looks like 'fell silent', matching 'reticent', but it means lock away.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the moneylender demanding his pound of flesh in The Merchant of Venice.

entries.clue: Start wandering around area to find geological features (6)

indicatorNotes.wandering around: a wanderer goes all over the place, and so do START's letters

annotation.surface: An instruction to begin rambling around a region looking at the rocks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like the instruction to begin, but it is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: rock layers laid down over time are one kind of geological feature.
